chunks: We have been borne in such a wrongful and thank-less period wherein the virtuous is deemed vicious and the oppressor goes on advancing in his excesses. We do not make use of what we know and do not discover what we do not know. We do not fear calamity till it befalls.

key_terms.الْمُحْسِنُ: the virtuous / the doer of good
key_terms.دَهْرٍ عَنُودٍ: a difficult, stubborn, or unyielding era
key_terms.زَمَانٍ كَنُودٍ: a time that is hard to bear or endure

ai.seo_question: What characterizes the 'difficult era' described in Nahj al-Balagha regarding moral inversion and societal negligence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) characterizes this era as 'Dahr 'Unud' (a stubborn, unyielding time) where societal norms invert, rewarding oppression and penalizing virtue, reflecting the post-Uthmanic political turmoil. This passage serves as a diagnostic of spiritual stagnation, where the community fails to act on known truths or seek new guidance, leaving them vulnerable to sudden divine retribution.

en.sayed-ali-raza: We have been borne in such a wrongful and thank-less period wherein the virtuous is deemed vicious and the oppressor goes on advancing in his excesses. We do not make use of what we know and do not discover what we do not know. We do not fear calamity till it befalls.
